style: Comprehensive meaningful blend (interpretive text) + amplified study form; bare transliterations in amp with Strong's carried in notes; em-dashes used sparingly; transliterations ASCII-normalized relative to the lexicon's spellings; 'the LORD' for YHWH; deity pronouns capitalized.
chapterNote: The psalm of the pit and the scroll. It opens with the testimony every believer eventually owns: in waiting I waited -- the doubled Hebrew of long, deliberate hope -- and He bent down, heard, and hauled me up out of the roaring pit and the swamp-clay, stood my feet on rock, and put a new song in my mouth that turns spectators into trusters. At its center stands the passage Hebrews 10 takes up as the very words of Christ entering the world: sacrifice and offering You did not desire -- my ears You have dug open -- then I said, 'Here I am, I have come; in the scroll of the book it is written of me: I delight to do Your will, O My God, and Your torah is deep inside Me.' The animal blood that could never take away sin gives way to the obedient Son whose whole life is the offering (Hebrews 10:5-10). The back half of the psalm returns to the ground where believers actually live: righteousness proclaimed to the great assembly with unsealed lips; then fresh trouble -- evils past counting, iniquities overtaking, heart failing -- and the old cry made new: be pleased, O LORD, to deliver me; let those who love Your salvation say continually, 'The LORD be magnified!' The last verse is the whole posture of faith: I am poor and needy, yet the Lord is thinking about me. Do not delay, O my God.

1.text: For the choir director. A psalm of David. In waiting I waited for the LORD, and He bent down to me and heard my cry.
1.amp: To the chief Musician [natsach], A Psalm [mizmor] of David. I waited patiently ['In waiting I waited', qavah qavah, the KJV margin] for the LORD [YHWH]; and He inclined [natah -- bent, stretched down] unto me, and heard [shama] my cry [shavah].
1.notes: The Hebrew doubles the cord-taut hope-verb: qavoh qivviti (H6960), waiting waited -- endurance stacked on endurance. And the answer is posture before action: natah (H5186), God bending down to the crier's level, the listening lean of Psalm 130:2 fulfilled.

2.text: He brought me up out of the pit of roaring ruin, out of the mire and the clay; He set my feet upon a rock and made my steps firm under me.
2.amp: He brought me up [alah] also out of an horrible pit ['a pit of noise', bor shaon, the KJV margin -- the roaring cistern], out of the miry [yaven] clay [tit], and set [qum] my feet [regel] upon a rock [sela], and established [kun] my goings [ashur -- my steps].
2.notes: The bor shaon (H953, H7588), the cistern of roaring -- a pit with noise in it, ruin you can hear -- and the yaven tit (H3121, H2916), bottomless swamp-clay that gives no footing to climb by. Rescue is total reversal: alah (H5927) up, sela (H5553) underfoot, and kun (H3559) applied to each ashur (H838), every single step firmed.

3.text: And He put a new song in my mouth, a praise-song to our God. Many will see it and fear, and will put their trust in the LORD.
3.amp: And He has put [natan] a new [chadash] song [shir] in my mouth [peh], even praise [tehillah] unto our God [Elohim]: many [rav] shall see [raah] it, and fear [yare], and shall trust [batach] in the LORD [YHWH].
3.notes: The shir chadash (H7892, H2319): rescue composes its own music, given (natan, H5414) along with the deliverance. And testimony evangelizes -- the watching rav (H7227) move from raah to yare to batach (H982), seeing to awe to leaning trust: one man's pit-story becomes many men's conversion (cf. Psalm 51:13).

4.text: Oh the blessedness of the man who has made the LORD his confidence, who does not turn toward the proud or those who fall away to a lie.
4.amp: Blessed [esher] is that man [geber] that makes [sum] the LORD [YHWH] his trust [mivtach -- his confidence, his security], and respects [panah -- turns toward] not the proud [rahab], nor such as turn aside [sut] to lies [kazab].
4.notes: mivtach (H4009): trust as the thing one's security is actually built on, deliberately sum (H7760), placed. The alternatives are named -- the rehabim, the arrogant powers, and the kazab (H3577), the lie in all its market forms; blessedness includes what the face refuses to panah (H6437) toward.

5.text: Many things You have done, O LORD my God -- Your wonderful works and Your thoughts toward us. There is none to compare with You. If I tried to declare and recount them, they are too many to number.
5.amp: Many [rav], O LORD [YHWH] my God [Elohim], are Your wonderful [pala] works which You have done [asah], and Your thoughts [machashabah -- plans, purposes] which are toward us: they cannot be set in order ['none can order them unto thee', arak, the KJV margin] unto You: if I would declare [nagad] and speak [dabar] of them, they are more [atsam] than can be numbered [saphar].
5.notes: Two uncountables: the pala-works (H6381) already done, and the machashabot (H4284) -- God's thoughts aimed 'to us-ward', the same treasure Psalm 139:17-18 weighed against the sand. arak (H6186) fails, saphar (H5608) fails: the ledger of grace breaks the bookkeeper.

6.text: Sacrifice and grain offering You did not desire -- my ears You have dug open; burnt offering and sin offering You did not require.
6.amp: Sacrifice [zebach] and offering [minchah -- the grain gift] You did not desire [chaphets]; mine ears [ozen] have You opened ['digged', karah, the KJV margin]: burnt offering [olah] and sin offering [chataah] have You not required [shaal].
6.notes: All four offering-classes named and set aside -- zebach, minchah, olah, chataah -- for the thing they always pointed at: karah ozen (H3738, H241), ears dug open, obedience excavated where ritual had silted in (cf. 1 Samuel 15:22). The Septuagint renders it 'a body You prepared for Me,' and Hebrews 10:5 carries that reading onto the lips of Christ entering the world.

7.text: Then I said, 'Look -- I have come. In the scroll of the book it is written concerning Me.
7.amp: Then said [amar] I, 'Lo, I come [bo]: in the volume [megillah -- the roll] of the book [sepher] it is written [kathab] of Me,'
7.notes: hinneh bati -- 'Behold, I have come': the willing self-offer that replaces the four offerings of verse 6. The megillat sepher (H4039, H5612) is the scroll where the mission stands pre-written -- for David, the covenant charter; for the Son, the whole counsel of God He came to perform (cf. Hebrews 10:7; Luke 24:44).

8.text: I delight to do Your will, O My God; Your law is deep within Me, in My inmost being.'
8.amp: 'I delight [chaphets] to do [asah] Your will [ratson], O my God [Elohim]: yea, Your law [torah] is within ['in the midst of my bowels', tavek meah, the KJV margin] my heart.'
8.notes: The chaphets (H2654) God had for no sacrifice (v. 6) is here answered by a Servant whose chaphets is the ratson (H7522) itself -- delight meeting delight. torah be-tok meai (H8432, H4578): the law not consulted but resident, in the inmost organs -- the new covenant's promise embodied (cf. Jeremiah 31:33), and the sentence Hebrews says sanctified us once for all (cf. Hebrews 10:9-10).

9.text: I have proclaimed the glad news of righteousness in the great assembly; look, I have not sealed my lips -- O LORD, You Yourself know it.
9.amp: I have preached [basar -- proclaimed as good news] righteousness [tsedek] in the great [rav] congregation [qahal]: lo, I have not refrained [kala -- restrained, sealed] my lips [saphah], O LORD [YHWH], You know [yada].
9.notes: basar (H1319) is the gospel-verb, to herald glad tidings: tsedek announced, not merely possessed. The double witness -- the qahal (H6951) heard it, and YHWH atah yadata, You know -- an appeal to the only audit that matters (cf. Romans 10:15).

10.text: I have not hidden Your righteousness inside my heart; I have spoken out Your faithfulness and Your salvation; I have not concealed Your covenant love and Your truth from the great assembly.
10.amp: I have not hid [kasah] Your righteousness [tsedaqah] within [tavek] my heart [leb]; I have declared [amar] Your faithfulness [emunah] and Your salvation [teshuah]: I have not concealed [kachad] Your lovingkindness [chesed] and Your truth [emeth] from the great [rav] congregation [qahal].
10.notes: Five glories un-hidden: tsedaqah, emunah, teshuah, chesed, emeth -- the full vocabulary of God's character made public property. kasah and kachad (H3680, H3582), the two hiding-verbs, both negated: what verse 8 internalized, verses 9-10 broadcast; the torah within becomes testimony without.

11.text: So You, O LORD -- do not withhold Your deep compassions from me; let Your covenant love and Your truth guard me continually.
11.amp: Withhold [kala] not Your tender mercies [rachamim -- womb-deep compassions] from me, O LORD [YHWH]: let Your lovingkindness [chesed] and Your truth [emeth] continually [tamid] preserve [natsar -- keep watch over] me.
11.notes: The elegant turn: 'I did not kala my lips (v. 9); do not kala (H3607) Your rachamim (H7356).' The unheld tongue appeals to the unheld mercy. chesed and emeth, just proclaimed to the qahal, are requested back as a personal guard detail, natsar (H5341), tamid.

12.text: For evils past counting have closed around me; my iniquities have overtaken me until I cannot lift my eyes. They are more than the hairs of my head, and my heart has abandoned me.
12.amp: For innumerable [mispar ayin] evils [ra] have compassed [aphaph -- closed in around] me about: mine iniquities [avon] have taken hold [nasag -- overtaken] upon me, so that I am not able [yakol] to look up [raah]; they are more [atsam] than the hairs [saarah] of mine head [rosh]: therefore my heart [leb] fails ['forsaketh', azab, the KJV margin] me.
12.notes: The rescued singer of verse 2 is back in deep water -- the psalms never pretend one deliverance ends the war. aphaph (H661) is the closing ring of Jonah's prayer, and nasag (H5381) the overtaking: his own avon (H5771) running him down like pursuers. The count that failed for mercies (v. 5) now fails for sins -- more than the head's hairs -- and the leb azab (H5800), the heart itself deserts its post.

13.text: Be pleased, O LORD, to deliver me; O LORD, hurry to my help.
13.amp: Be pleased [ratsah], O LORD [YHWH], to deliver [natsal -- snatch away] me: O LORD, make haste [chush] to help me.
13.notes: ratsah (H7521), the acceptance-verb of sacrifices: may my rescue please You -- deliverance asked as something God would enjoy doing. chush (H2363), the hurry-verb of Psalm 22:19: waiting faith (v. 1) is still allowed to pray 'run.'

14.text: Let those who seek my life to sweep it away be ashamed and confounded together; let those who wish me evil be driven backward and disgraced.
14.amp: Let them be ashamed [bosh] and confounded [chapher] together [yachad] that seek [baqash] after my soul [nephesh] to destroy [saphah -- sweep away] it; let them be driven [sug] backward [achor] and put to shame [kalam] that wish me evil [ra].
14.notes: The imprecation asks precisely for reversal, not revenge: bosh, chapher, sug achor (H954, H2659, H5472) -- faces fallen, plans stalled, momentum thrown into reverse. The soul-sweepers (saphah, H5595) meet the recoil their own pursuit generates.

15.text: Let those who say to me, 'Aha! Aha!' be left desolate as the wages of their shame.
15.amp: Let them be desolate [shamem] for a reward [eqev -- as the consequence] of their shame [bosheth] that say [amar] unto me, 'Aha [heach], aha.'
15.notes: heach (H1889) is malice's little grunt of satisfaction -- gloating compressed to one syllable, doubled. eqev (H6118), the heel-word: desolation arriving as the natural next footstep of their own bosheth (H1322); the mockery writes its own invoice.

16.text: But let all who go seeking You rejoice and be glad in You; let the lovers of Your salvation say continually, 'The LORD be magnified!'
16.amp: Let all those that seek [baqash] You rejoice [sus] and be glad [samach] in You: let such as love [ahab] Your salvation [teshuah] say [amar] continually [tamid], 'The LORD [YHWH] be magnified [gadal].'
16.notes: The counter-community to verse 14's hunters: the baqash-ers of God rather than of a victim's life. Their tamid-refrain, yigdal YHWH (H1431), 'the LORD be magnified,' is the healthy soul's default setting -- and note whom it belongs to: those who ahab (H157) His teshuah, lovers of the rescue itself.

17.text: As for me, I am poor and needy -- yet the Lord is thinking about me. You are my help and my deliverer; do not delay, O my God.
17.amp: But I am poor [ani -- afflicted] and needy [evyon]; yet the Lord [Adonai] thinks [chashab -- reckons, plans] upon me: you are my help [ezrah] and my deliverer [palat]; make no tarrying [achar -- do not delay], O my God [Elohim].
17.notes: The psalm's whole theology in its last breath: ani ve-evyon (H6041, H34), the honest self-assessment -- and Adonai chashab li (H2803), the Lord's thoughts occupied with ME, one of the uncountable machashabot of verse 5 with my name on it. The final word is faith's impatience made reverent: al-teachar (H309), do not delay.
